title: NAT on Junos: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Private addresses can't travel across the internet. N A T fixes that. But on Junos, there's a catch.

lines.t: Private addresses can't reach the internet

scenes.heading: The visitor parking pass
scenes.narration: Imagine an apartment block that only lets resident cars into the lot. A visitor's van is turned away until it's given a pass. The pass swaps a private plate for a public one. Visitors arriving get sent to the right flat. A permanent reserved space is another option.

scenes.heading: Two parts to every setup
scenes.narration: On Junos, you always need two parts. The N A T rule changes the address. And a security policy allows the traffic. Without both, nothing flows. Write the NAT rule. Add a security policy. Check it worked.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps to avoid. One public address can serve thousands of devices with source N A T. Destination N A T and static N A T are not the same thing. And a N A T rule doesn't permit traffic, you still need a policy.

items.wrong: Every device needs its own public IP
items.right: One public address can serve thousands

items.wrong: Destination NAT and static NAT are identical
items.right: Destination is often per-port; static is one-to-one

items.wrong: A NAT rule lets traffic through
items.right: You still need a security policy

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos NAT lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Source N A T rewrites outbound traffic, and destination N A T rewrites inbound. Static N A T is a permanent one to one mapping. A N A T rule needs a matching security policy. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos NAT lab.

points.t: NAT rule needs a security policy
